title: Uniform lower-tail amplitude of proper direct image on the qcqs constructible finite-Tor hull
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, and an admissible commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$: a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with exactly the discrete or induced $\ell$-adic topological condensed-ring convention of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the finite constant scalar-model constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, $q:Y\to S$ proper and $f:X\to Y$ proper. Write $\mathcal L_X=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))$ for the full replete triangulated hull closed under small coproducts in $D_X$ [sk-def-localizing-closure]. There exists $c\in\mathbf N$, independent of $a$ and $K$, such that for every $a\in\mathbf Z$ and every $K\in\mathcal L_X$,
$$H^r\bigl(Rf_*\tau_{<a}K\bigr)=0\qquad(r\geq a+c).$$
Here $\tau_{<a}=\tau_{\leq a-1}$ is the standard good truncation [def-kun-truncations]. The truncation and $Rf_*$ are taken in the ordinary ambient derived categories; the truncated object is not required to remain in $\mathcal L_X$. In particular, the assertion concerns lower tails which need not be derived complete. No field, characteristic, Noetherian or finite-dimensional-base hypothesis is imposed.

Agent formulation of the relative cohomological estimate, not an attribution of its full scope to Bhatt–Scholze 6.7.2 or 6.8.15.

proof.text: For $T=X,Y$, apply the sheaf tensor theorem to $\mathcal A=\Ab$ on the chosen small pro-étale site. It gives a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian sheaf category, with additive tensor. The module-object theorem therefore makes $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ Grothendieck abelian. In particular its filtered colimits are exact. Coproducts are filtered colimits of finite direct sums, so are exact. The termwise-coproduct theorem identifies coproducts in $D(\mathcal A_T)$ with termwise sums of representing complexes. Exactness then gives $H^i(\bigoplus_t K_t)\simeq\bigoplus_tH^i(K_t)$: apply the sum to the kernel, image and cokernel sequences defining cohomology.

source.place: (2), first paragraph: ambient module-derived coproducts and their cohomology

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P_X$ be the weak Serre coproduct class defined in the cited heart estimate and put $\mathcal C_X=\{K\mid H^i(K)\in\mathcal P_X\text{ for every }i\}$. This class is replete and shift-stable. For a triangle $B\to C\to D\to B[1]$ with $B,D\in\mathcal C_X$, its long exact sequence expresses $H^i(C)$ as an extension of $\operatorname{coker}(H^{i-1}(D)\to H^i(B))$ by $\ker(H^i(D)\to H^{i+1}(B))$. Both belong to $\mathcal P_X$ by its defining closure properties, so $C\in\mathcal C_X$; rotation gives the other two-out-of-three cases. Step 1 and coproduct closure of $\mathcal P_X$ make $\mathcal C_X$ closed under all ambient small sums. Every $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ object has constructible cohomology, hence belongs to $\mathcal C_X$. The intersection definition of $\mathcal L_X$ now gives $\mathcal L_X\subseteq\mathcal C_X$. Finally any good truncation of such a $K$ still has cohomology in $\mathcal P_X$, since it retains the original cohomology in the retained range and is zero elsewhere.

source.place: (2), first paragraph: pass from generators to cohomology of every object in the localizing hull

proof.text: Choose $d\geq0$ from the heart estimate. Thus $Rf_*(M[0])$ has no cohomology above $d$ for every $M\in\mathcal P_X$. The underived module-object pushforward is additive and left exact. Grothendieck abelianness from Step 1 gives K-injective resolutions, and the triangulated derived-functor theorem applies to its actual total right derived functor. Fix $a\in\mathbf Z$, $K\in\mathcal L_X$ and set $L=\tau_{<a}K$. For every $n\geq0$, the complex $L_n=\tau_{\geq-n}L$ is bounded, has cohomology in $\mathcal P_X$ by Step 2, and has no cohomology above $a-1$. Bounded heart-amplitude dévissage, with upper endpoint $a-1$, gives $H^r(Rf_*L_n)=0$ for every $r>a-1+d$, uniformly in $n$. If $-n>a-1$, $L_n=0$ and the same bound holds.

source.place: (2), first paragraph: use the uniform heart estimate on every bounded lower truncation of the tail

proof.text:
Apply the module-object Postnikov–Roos theorem to the morphism $f$ and the ordinary ambient object $L$. With $B_n=Rf_*L_n$ it gives a distinguished triangle
$$Rf_*L\longrightarrow P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\longrightarrow(Rf_*L)[1],\qquad P=\prod_{n\geq0}B_n,$$
and $H^j(P)\simeq\prod_{n\geq0}H^j(B_n)$ for every $j$. Step 3 therefore gives $H^j(P)=0$ for $j>a-1+d$. If $r>a+d$, both $r-1$ and $r$ satisfy this inequality. The exact segment $H^{r-1}(P)\to H^r(Rf_*L)\to H^r(P)$ has zero end terms, so $H^r(Rf_*L)=0$. This is an application to all unbounded module-object complexes: it does not require $L$ to be in the hull or to be derived complete.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit), the Roos triangle; Tag 07KC (lemma-products), product cohomology; actual pro-étale module-object Postnikov cone supplied by the cited node

proof.text: Take $c=d+1\in\mathbf N$. If $r\geq a+c$, then $r>a+d$, and Step 4 gives the required vanishing. The chosen $d$ and hence $c$ depend only on the fixed morphisms and coefficients, not on $a$ or $K$. Zero objects, empty schemes and empty fibres cause no exception: the same closure and truncation arguments give zero complexes. The argument takes every sum, truncation and derived image in the ordinary ambient category, exactly as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NY-0996b821e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full: all 5 steps, every cited statement, the new node, the parent lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-localizing-coproducts (its Step 4 uses this item) and blueprint det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement proof (2). There is no repair note, the item is not dropped and there is no SGA citation. Step 1 holds: module objects in Sh(proét,Ab) are Grothendieck, sums are exact, and H^i commutes with sums. Step 2: the cohomology class C_X meets def-weil-triangulated-subcategory (extension, shift, zero), is closed under sums by Step 1, and contains Dctf, so L_X is inside C_X. Truncations keep their cohomology in P_X. Step 3: f_* is additive and left exact, and K-injectives give a triangulated Rf_*. Bounded-heart dévissage applies to tau_{>=-n}tau_{<=a-1}K with upper endpoint a-1. Step 4: module Postnikov–Roos gives the Roos triangle and H^j preserving N-products, so r>a+d gives vanishing. Step 5: c=d+1. The new node lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-serre-heart-bound is statement-only and self-contained. Its P_X is the weak Serre coproduct closure that Step 2 needs. It is a degree-0 bound, strictly smaller than the item, not a restatement. Small cases: id gives d=0; for finite Lambda, P_X lies in nu^*(torsion étale), so proper base change and fibre cd give d=2·(fibre dim), including l=p; P^1 with Q_l gives d=2. I found no counterexample, and the general proof is honest downstream work. No duplicate: the existing heart nodes (sk-lem-proper-heart-bound, det-proper-heart-bound-*, lem-sfb-noetherian-proper-heart-uniform-bound, lem-sfb-proper-serre-heart-continuous, thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin) all assume a field, a Noetherian base, l≠p, finite coefficients or étale origin. I accept the declared generic tool_uses. No fixes.
